Record.Get is optimized for retrieving a single record based on primary key values.
Record.Find('-') and Record.Find('+') use self-tuning TOP X calls and are best for reading when you might not need all records.
Record.FindSet is optimized for reading the complete set of records in specified filters and ranges.
Each CalcFields or CalcSums call requires a separate SQL statement unless the result is cached from a recent identical calculation.
SetAutoCalcFields method optimizes performance by calculating FlowFields during record retrieval instead of in separate calls.
Using FindSet with var parameter and direct Modify or Delete avoids extra SQL statements compared to copying records.
ModifyAll and DeleteAll revert to individual SQL calls if triggers, event subscribers, security filtering, Media fields, or companion tables exist.
Business Central automatically buffers inserts to send them to SQL Server at one time, reducing server calls and improving performance.
Bulk inserts improve scalability by delaying actual insert until last moment, reducing table lock time especially for SIFT indexes.
Records are sent to SQL Server when COMMIT is called, MODIFY or DELETE is called, or FIND or CALC methods are called.
Bulk inserts are not used if code uses return value from INSERT call or if table contains BLOB fields or AutoIncrement properties.
Disable bulk inserts by setting BufferedInsertEnabled parameter to FALSE in CustomSettings.config file for troubleshooting.
Server data cache is shared by all users connected to same server instance.
GET, FIND, FINDSET, FINDLAST, COUNT, ISEMPTY, and CALCFIELDS methods use cache system.
Global cache is for all users; private cache is per user per company in transactional scope.
Default data cache size is 9 approximating 500 MB; increasing by one doubles the cache size.
Query objects do not use the cache system.
Query is an object used to specify set of data to read from Business Central database, supporting single or multiple tables with joins and totaling.
Sub-query is automatically added to SQL statement for each FlowField in query to retrieve all data in one request.
FlowFields cannot be used on virtual tables in queries because they cannot be automatically converted to SQL statements.
Covering index contains all output fields required by operation and greatly improves performance by retrieving only index data.
SIFT index supports queries with aggregated columns using Sum, Count, or Average methods when totals are part of key fields.
Query result sets are not guaranteed to be dynamic, unlike record result sets which are always dynamic.
SQL Server query optimizer can be overridden with query hints to enforce specific execution plans for SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE statements.
SQL optimization covers compatibility level, data access, table keys, bulk inserts, and query hints

Time to complete loop through record subset depends on subset size; inefficient retrieval causes performance degradation.
Define keys supporting code execution; specify correct keys to retrieve subset efficiently on SQL Server.

Column selectivity determines SQL Server index choice; low selectivity columns have few unique values, high selectivity have many.

Query hints are strategies to override SQL Server execution plans when the query optimizer may make suboptimal choices.

The admin center provides a portal for administrators to view and work with production and sandbox environments on the tenant.
Dynamics 365 Administrator and Dynamics 365 Business Central Administrator roles authorize access to the admin center.
Internal admins with Dynamics 365 Business Central Administrator role can access the admin center from Business Central or via direct URL.
Partner organizations must set up a GDAP relationship with required roles to access customer admin centers.
Delegated administrators do not need a license assigned or be a guest user to access customer admin centers.
Support contact details, notification recipients, Application Insights keys, and authorized Microsoft Entra apps should be removed when switching partners.
Delegated administrators and organization administrators with D365 BACKUP/RESTORE permission set assigned in the environment can restore.
Only paid subscribers can restore environments. Maximum 10 restores per calendar month per environment and restore only to 28 days prior.
Restored environment must stay within same Azure region and localization as original. Production restores to Production or Sandbox; Sandbox restores only to Sandbox.
Restoration restores environment to the major/minor version it was on at restore point. Cannot restore to versions in grace or enforced update periods.
Development extensions from Visual Studio Code are removed during sandbox restoration. Per-tenant extensions depending on them are also unavailable.
Marketplace and Business Central apps automatically receive latest available hotfixes even if the hotfix post-dates the restore point.
Microsoft Entra app registrations, status and permissions restore to their restore-point state. Previously authorized apps are not restored.
Update window and Application Insights connection string from source environment at restore start time are retained on target, not restored to historical values.
The Capacity page shows total database storage usage and details about storage used by every environment on the tenant.
Premium and Essential subscriptions include one production environment and three sandbox environments at no extra charge.
Each extra production environment purchased adds three more sandbox environments and increases shared storage capacity by 4 GB.
Extra storage capacity per license: Premium 3 GB, Essential 2 GB, Device 1 GB, Partner Sandbox 5 GB.
Exceeding storage quota does not interrupt existing environments but blocks creation or copying of new environments until quota is reduced or more capacity is purchased.
Exceeding environment count limits also blocks creation or copying of environments until you reduce or purchase more capacity.
Files and Blob data stored in the database, including Tenant Media and Tenant Media Thumbnails tables, count toward overall database storage capacity.
Administrators can limit user access to specific environments by changing permissions or removing users' access.
Exports Business Central online database as BACPAC files to Azure storage container
Customer must have paid Business Central subscription to request database export
D365 BACKUP/RESTORE permission set must be assigned in the environment to export
Maximum 10 database exports allowed per month per environment
Only Standard general-purpose v2 Azure storage accounts supported, not Premium or V1
SAS signature requires minimum 72-hour expiration window from export initiation
BACPAC files exported from customer-managed encrypted environments use storage account encryption
Microsoft does not support creating working on-premises environment from downloaded BACPAC
Business Central environments can link to Power Platform environments of the same type for inherited settings
Cannot delete a Business Central environment if linked to a Power Platform environment
Copy and Restore operations do not link the target environment to Power Platform as part of the operation
Internal admin with access to the admin center and permissions to update Power Platform environment properties required
Only Power Platform environments in Ready state, matching environment type, and not already linked are available for linking
Unlinking disables inherited settings but preserves existing integrations like Power Automate flows
Default update window excludes 8 PM to 6 AM local time; can be changed after environment creation
Create environment copy with all per-tenant and Marketplace extensions installed in original environment.
Copied environment runs on same application version as original environment.
Linked Power Platform environment is not copied; new environment will not be linked.
In Admin Center select Environments then choose the environment to copy.
On Environment Details page choose Copy action.
In Copy environment pane specify environment type and name for new environment.
Choose Create action to start the copy process.
Sandbox environments with Preview Marketplace apps cannot be copied to Production; update or uninstall Preview apps first.
Deleted environments enter a retention period lasting 14 days called soft delete before permanent hard delete.
During the 14-day retention period, you can fully recover the environment and all its data.
Environments with Creating Failed or Removing Failed status are permanently deleted immediately without retention.
Soft-deleted environments are automatically renamed with a date-time suffix format yyMMddHHmmssff to avoid naming conflicts.
Soft-deleted environments do not receive updates but remain in the update schedule until permanently deleted.
When recovering an environment, pending updates scheduled during deletion are applied unless you reschedule them.
You can recover a production environment exceeding quota by one extra environment; return within quota within 30 days.
Environments linked to Power Platform cannot be deleted without unlinking first.
Environments move between Microsoft Entra tenants during business consolidations, acquisitions, mergers, or partner demo transfers to customer tenants.
Source tenant internal admin initiates transfer in Business Central admin center by selecting environments, specifying destination tenant ID and transfer date/time.
Destination tenant internal admin accepts transfer within 8 hours via Receive Environments, optionally renaming environments to avoid duplicates.
Only internal administrators can execute environment transfer operations; delegated admins cannot use this feature.
All source tenant users are disconnected when transfer starts and post-transfer setup is required before environment use, typically requiring up to 30 minutes downtime.
Users added to environment in source tenant are not migrated; they must be recreated in destination tenant and user personalizations are lost.
Environments linked to Power Platform cannot be transferred; must unlink Business Central environment from Power Platform first.
Transfer requests remain valid 2 weeks if accepted within 8 hours of creation; requests not accepted within 8 hours get status Skipped.
Environment name is part of URL and changing it restarts the environment.
Select Environments, choose environment to rename, select Rename option.
Enter new name on Rename environment page and select Rename button.
Environment state changes to Preparing/Rename Scheduled then back to Active when complete.
Old environment name is no longer accessible; new name available immediately.
Renaming affects web client URL, deep links, integrations, mobile apps, Power BI, Excel add-ins.
Browser cache, CI/CD pipelines, launch.json files, and external integrations require manual updates.
Assign Microsoft Entra group to environment to restrict access to group members; direct and indirect members can sign in, but not group members cannot.
Internal administrators can freely sign in to all environments regardless of assigned security group; delegated admin access is controlled by Partner access setting.
To assign security group, select environment on Environments page, then select Define or Modify under Security Group, search for and select group, select Save.
Essentials users can only open companies with User Experience set to Essentials; Premium users can open any company but cannot use Premium-only features in Essentials companies.
Up to 10 Microsoft Entra tenants can be allowlisted per environment for delegated administrator and multitenant application access.
Partner access settings are preserved during environment copy, restore, and transfer operations; post-transfer, settings should be updated if destination tenant has different partners.
To manage partner access, select environment, select Modify for Partner access, toggle Allow partner access switch, control access to all or specific partner tenants, select Save.
A Business Central environment is built as a collection of apps including Microsoft and non-Microsoft apps from Marketplace.
Apps can be installed as Global App, Per-Tenant Extension, or DEV extension.
The Manage Apps page in the admin center supports viewing, uploading, installing, updating, and uninstalling apps depending on app type.
You cannot install new global apps from the Admin Center; install them from marketplace.microsoft.com instead.
Global app updates from Marketplace are applied immediately by default; schedule them during the next update window to minimize user disruption.
Per-Tenant Extension installations can be scheduled immediately, during the next update window, or during the next minor or major update.
Uninstalling an app can optionally delete application data in fields and tables; data recovery requires point-in-time restore.
Preview versions of Marketplace apps can only be installed on sandbox environments using a PreviewKey URL parameter from the publisher.
Billable agent capabilities include Expense Agent (preview), Payables Agent, Sales Order Agent, and AI development toolkit (preview) design and coding.
Copilot Credits are the billing units for consumption-based AI interactions and tasks in agents, with cost varying by agent type and features used.
Expense Agent charges 50 Copilot Credits per uploaded receipt regardless of resulting expense line count.
Sales Order Agent typical process costs 14 Copilot Credits base (analyze email, check availability, create quote/order, generate response) plus optional charges for attachments.
Payables Agent charges 50 Copilot Credits per invoice processing plus 5 per invoice line for extraction and intelligent matching.
Two billing models available: prepaid capacity purchased through Microsoft 365 or Partner Center, or pay-as-you-go linked to Azure subscription.
Prepaid capacity automatically consumed from default Power Platform environment; admins can allocate portions to specific environments through Power Platform admin center.
For pay-as-you-go, link Business Central environment to Power Platform environment configured with Azure subscription.
Manage Sessions page allows viewing information about active sessions and canceling selected sessions.
Canceling a session sometimes is the only way to unblock a customer when a long-running report locks data.
To cancel session, select it from the list and choose Cancel selected sessions.
To restart environment, go to Manage Sessions page and choose Restart Environment action.
All users must be signed out of all companies before restarting an environment.
Notification recipients receive email when major updates are available, updates succeed or fail, and extensions require compatibility changes.
Notifications are sent to all email addresses listed in the Notification recipients list of the admin center.
Up to 100 notification recipients can be added; use a distribution list to support more recipients.
Most environment lifecycle events posted to email are also posted to Microsoft 365 Message Center.
If an incompatible app is not uninstalled after 4-5 months of notifications, Microsoft force-uninstalls the app without deleting data.
Trial prospects must sign up for notifications to receive alerts about trial expiration and environment status.
Admin center provides telemetry for tenant environments enabling troubleshooting and support.
Telemetry tab shows top-level AL events and errors from telemetry stack.
Filter telemetry by selecting base point-in-time, time range, message type, and environment.
Helps identify underlying problems such as simultaneous data modification by multiple users.
Enable richer telemetry by sending data to Microsoft Azure Application Insights.
Update window is the hours during the day when environment updates can occur within specified time zone.
Update must complete before update window ends or it cancels and reschedules seven days later.
Default update window is between 8 PM and 6 AM local time for environment country; minimum six hours required.
Schedule update by opening environment details, selecting Modify for Next Update, choosing target version, and picking date.
Can only update to versions higher than current version within current or next major version.
During update, all users and sign-in attempts blocked with maintenance message.
Cannot cancel updates on environments in Enforced Update Period for source version.
Notification recipients receive email when new version available and when update scheduled, except for preview versions.

Delegated administrators are partner company employees with GDAP relationship; Dynamics 365 Business Central Administrator role recommended.
Internal administrators have read-only access to all Business Central areas even after subscription cancellation.
Internal administrators need Business Central license to set up integrations or perform tasks beyond user management and data export.
License Administrator role required in Microsoft 365 admin center to manage subscription and assign licenses.
User Administrator role required in Microsoft 365 admin center to add or remove users from tenant.
Partners can log in as delegated administrator to set up and troubleshoot customer environments.
Switching partners requires removing reseller relationship, disabling delegated admin, clearing partner settings, and adding new partner.
Business Central is available in a limited number of markets; check Country/regional availability and supported languages documentation.
Users must have a work or school account tied to a Microsoft Entra tenant to use Business Central online.
Each Microsoft Entra tenant automatically receives some environments, each tied to a specific country and localization.
Environments can contain multiple companies representing legal entities or business units with separate accounting requirements.
All licensed users in a Microsoft Entra tenant can access all companies in each environment of that tenant.
Users from one Microsoft Entra tenant cannot access environments belonging to another Microsoft Entra tenant.
Admins can transfer environments between Microsoft Entra tenants if organizational structure changes over time.
Partners can create test environments for testing or pre-sales demonstrations.
Test environments based on free 30-day trials require CSP access in Partner Center.
In Partner Center, create new test customer with test domain like contoso.onmicrosoft.com.
Subscribe to Dynamics 365 Business Central Premium Trial providing 25 licenses for 30 days.
Create test user and assign 1 Premium license; may take 10 minutes for licenses to display.

Organizations can sign up for a free Business Central trial to explore the experience.
A 30-day trial is available without sample data, allowing users to add their own business data for evaluation.
Users can extend the trial period if 30 days are not enough to decide on a subscription.
Viral trials do not expire unless the prospect switches to the 30-day trial, provided users access Business Central frequently.
If an organization stops using Business Central, the administrator must remove the subscription in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
All customers, including trial organizations, can use sandbox environments for practicing without affecting production.
Strongly not recommended to use a free trial to run your business; contact a reselling partner to migrate data.
Event Viewer Application window displays SQL queries exceeding SqlLongRunningThreshold as warnings.
Default SqlLongRunningThreshold is 1000 milliseconds for identifying slow queries.
Long running queries with explicit AL code include AL call stack showing generated SQL.
AL call stack identifies specific AL method and line causing slow query execution.
Queries from triggers without code or GetPage calls do not include AL call stack.
Threshold can be set to different value without restarting server instance.
SQL Server Query Store captures history of queries, plans, and runtime statistics.
Query Store available in SQL Server 2016 and later and Azure SQL Database.
Tracks executions, average execution time, physical IO reads, and row counts per query.
Helps identify performance differences caused by query plan changes over time.
Simplifies troubleshooting by providing history of queries executed on database.
SmartSQL optimization performs all FlowField calculations on a page using a single SQL query, reducing network roundtrips to the database.
SmartSQL adds an OUTER APPLY clause to the SQL statement for each FlowField in the table.
To isolate FlowField query performance issues, run the Business Central administration tool and select the Disable SmartSQL checkbox in the Database section.
When SmartSQL is disabled, each FlowField calculation is performed as a separate SQL statement instead of being combined.
After identifying a slow FlowField subquery, create an index or enable the MaintainSIFTIndex property of the key to improve performance.
SmartSQL queries are not cached, which can amplify performance issues and disabling it does not require page customization or field visibility changes.
SAML2 token errors occur when the security token lifetime from Microsoft Entra ID has exceeded its default limit of 1 hour.
Users experience a connection lost error message when the SAML2 token validity period ends.
The server includes a configuration setting called ExtendedSecurityTokenLifetime that adds time to the security token lifetime.
To resolve token expiration issues, increase the ExtendedSecurityTokenLifetime setting on the Business Central server.
The Windows client times out after 9 or more hours of continuous connection, causing an ID4148 error that cannot be changed.
Resolve Windows client timeout by closing and reopening the client application.
The Business Central server requires Named Pipes and TCP/IP protocols to be enabled in SQL Server Configuration Manager for proper database connectivity.
In SQL Server Configuration Manager, expand the SQL Server Network Configuration node and select Protocols for MSSQLSERVER to verify or enable Named Pipes and TCP/IP.
If a protocol is disabled, right-click it and select Enable, then restart the Business Central server.
Windows Firewall must explicitly allow the SQL Server executable file sqlservr.exe as an exception to permit connections.
In Windows Firewall exceptions, add the SQL Server executable at C:\Program Files\Microsoft SQL Server\MSSQL*\MSSQL\Binn\sqlservr.exe.
When using a named database instance with the server and SQL Server on separate computers, the SQL Browser Service must be running on the SQL Server.
ClientServicesIdleClientTimeout on server controls inactive connection timeout; defaults to MaxValue (no limit).
SessionTimeout on web server controls inactive session timeout; defaults to 20 minutes.
Session closes based on whichever timeout setting has the shortest period between server and web server.
ClientServicesReconnectPeriod applies to Business Central 2022 version 20 and earlier only.
In Business Central 2023 and later, sessions terminate instantly when client loses connection; reconnection isn't supported.
Use Set-NAVServerConfiguration and Set-NAVWebServerInstanceConfiguration PowerShell commands to modify timeout settings.
If active session exists during timeout, server aborts current call stack, rolls back uncommitted transactions, and closes session.

Update affects on-premises, hosted, and private cloud deployments; Business Central online customers not affected.
After update users cannot sign in to add-in if redirect URI is not changed in Microsoft Entra app registration.
Sign in to Azure portal and go to Microsoft Entra ID App Registrations.
Select the Excel add-in app registration and go to Manifest.
Change redirect URI type from Web to Spa in the manifest.
Changes can be made at any time; existing add-in works with the new configuration.
Generally available. Two major releases occur every April and October.
Preview period starts one month before major release, typically March and September. Partner Sandbox tenants access early access preview alongside the entire update period.
Update period begins when major version is generally available, around first workday of April and October. New environments created on new major version.
Update period lasts five calendar months, ending early September for April releases and early March for October releases. Administrators can reschedule updates within this period.
Grace period lasts one month following the update period. During grace period, admins cannot reschedule updates to later dates, only to earlier dates or different major versions.
Enforced update period begins when grace period ends. Extensions causing update failures may be automatically uninstalled so updates succeed.
Cannot restore an environment to a version in its Grace or Enforced update period after updating to a later version succeeds.
Minor updates release monthly except April and October, containing critical improvements and regulatory updates. Generally available at start of each calendar month.
Server events are collected in Debug logs under Applications and Services Logs for DynamicsNAV Server and Common.
Debug logs are disabled by default and may be hidden in Event Viewer.
Open Event Viewer on the computer running the server.
Navigate to Applications and Services Logs > Microsoft > DynamicsNAV > Server or Common.
Show Analytic and Debug Logs from the View menu if Debug log is not visible.
Select Debug log and choose Enable Log from the Actions menu.
Default log size is 1028 KB; increase if needed based on event volume.
Table partitioning divides large tables across filegroups for faster maintenance, improved queries, and better performance via partition elimination.
Partitioning field must be included in the table's primary key in AL code; partitioning is configured in SQL Server after table publication.
Primary key fields cannot be added after an extension publishes to production; partitioning is limited to new extensions or existing ones with partitioning fields already in primary keys.
Compression reduces table size and improves I/O-intensive workload performance; CompressionType property lets you set Row, Page, or Unspecified compression.
In Business Central online, tables are compressed using Page compression by default.
Partitioning and compression can be combined for flexible data archiving on historical partitions without CPU overhead on active parts.
